topic: ZhiShi: A Rust Agent Harness for Security Research

key_points: AI agent toolkit: unified LLM API, agent loop, TUI, coding agent CLI
MIT-licensed TypeScript foundation (~98.7k stars); ZhiShi's loop engine is built on pi-agent-core
Established the 'generic agent harness' pattern ZhiShi customizes for security research
Open-source agent harness for building reliable AI agents (Show HN)
Focuses on reliability/observability of agent loops, not security-research-specific tooling
Local AI pentesting agent running on a smartphone (Show HN, 120 pts)
Contrast: consumer mobile pentest assistant vs. ZhiShi's desktop researcher workbench
Agentic AI pentesting with Strix — benchmark results across 18 LLM models
Positions LLM-driven pentest automation as an emerging, measurable field
Argues the agent harness should live outside the sandbox (182 pts)
Architectural debate relevant to ZhiShi's environment-fusion + boundary-guard design

stats.fact: ZhiShi v1.4.7, AGPL-3.0, 69 stars / 4 forks (as of research date), Node >=22 desktop app (Tauri/Rust shell wrapping a TypeScript loop engine)
Claims CTF completion: Pwnable.kr 100%, Hacker101 98%, HackThisSite 96%, ROP Emporium 91%, VulnHub 90%
CVE-2026-34621: Adobe Acrobat Reader prototype pollution, CVSS 8.6 HIGH — featured as full exploit-chain reproduction
CVE-2026-0961: Wireshark BLF file parser crash (DoS), CVSS 5.5, claimed in ZhiShi's CVE log
Project claims 200+ vulnerabilities found via white-box auditing, 7 in-flight Microsoft submissions, plus Chrome/Firefox browser vuln analysis
Unit tests: 2370+ passing; smoke/dogfood runs across four research domains (binary, pentest, whitebox, ai-security)
Loop engine based on @earendil-works/pi-agent-core (MIT), itself ~98.7k stars

angles: Rust/Tauri desktop shell + TypeScript loop engine: the 'Rust agent harness' label is really a Rust-compiled Tauri app wrapping a Node/TS research engine — a nuance worth clarifying in the review
Environment-fusion as the differentiator: harness owns env lifecycle (Docker/VMware/Hyper-V/VirtualBox/SSH) instead of bundling tools — 'native tools live in the environment' philosophy
Evidence-anchored research archive: findings must cite V# evidence refs, falsify/correct trails, and a confidence floor (<0.60 not reported) — unusually rigorous for an agent harness
Safety/authorization posture: explicit legal-authorization disclaimer, out-of-bounds modal for host writes, credential redaction, hard tool whitelist — relevant for a security tool review
AI-security as a first-class research domain alongside binary exploitation and pentesting
Verifiability question: CVEs and CTF completion rates are self-reported; review should treat claims as vendor-provided until independently reproduced
